gallery.title: File:Ellora Cave 12 si0241.jpg
gallery.description:
Goddess. Third floor, Cave 12, Ellora

Both the goddess and her surrounding niche were originally
painted, as shown from the traces which remain. Goddess iconography (such as Tara, Mahamayuri, etc) relates to the development of Esoteric Buddhism towards the end of the active period of Buddhist influence in India.

gallery.title: File:Ellora Cave 16 si0300.jpg
gallery.description:
Ramayana Panel. Kailasanatha Temple, Ellora
This panel is situated at the southwest corner, ground floor level, of the temple.

gallery.title: File:Ellora Cave 32 si0339.jpg
gallery.description:
Mahavira. Cave 32, Ellora
Mahavira, the historical founder of the Jain religion, is flanked by divinities of prosperity (Matanga, male, photo left) and generosity (Sidaika, female, photo right).
Cave 32 dates to the early 9th century. The similarity to Buddhist
iconography is obvious, but Jain tirthankaras can be distinguished
by the nudity of their figures.

La grotte jaïne "Indra Sabha" (Ellora, Inde) 
La tour pyramidale du sanctuaire monolithique de la grotte 32 de culte jaïn à Ellora

La tour pyramidale est composée de gradins ornés de répliques de sanctuaires en bois à toit en berceau, elle reflète la cosmogonie jaïn.
